To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

composite carbon molecular sieve membranes were prepared by pyrolysis of polyimides with thermally decomposable sulfonic acid salt (SO3 NH(C2 H5)3) or hexafluoro isopropylidne (–C(C F3)2) group, which displayed the highest gas permance and reasonable ideal separation factors for oxygen/nitrogen or carbon dioxide/nitrogen separation.

CMS membranes prepared from polyimide with sulfonic acid salt (SO3–NH(C2H3)3) and hexafluoroiso-propylidene groups (–C(Cf3)2–), by pyrolysis at 873 K for 1 h, exhibited high O2 and CO₂ gas permeances with reasonable ideal separation factors for the O₂/N₂ and CO₂/N₂ separations.
the CMS composite membrane derived from the sulfonated polyimide containing the hexafluoro-isopropylidne group displayed the highest gas permselectivity among the composite CMS membranes studied.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation of CMS composite membranes by pyrolysis of the polyimides with thermally decomposable functional groups, such as sulfonic acid salt or –C(CF2)2–, for gas separations.
the synthesis and gas permeation properties of composite CMS membranes derived from polyimides containing sulfonic acid tri- ethylammonium salt and/or hexa fluor isopropylid ene groups.
the preparation of CMS membranes by the pyrolysis of precursor composite membranes derived from polyimides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a combination of sulfonic acid salt groups and hexafluoro-isopropylidenediamine moieties in the polyimide precursor would be a good candidate for preparation of composite CMS membranes with high gas permeances and reasonably high separation factors.
the CMS membranes prepared from the precursor polyimides containing thermally decomposable functional groups are promising for the O2/N2, CO2/N2, and CO2/H2 separations in the gas permeation process.

the polyimide precursor membrane with both the thermall decomposable groups is an excellent precursor for the preparation of composite CMS membranes with high gas permeances and reasonably high gas separation factors for O/N and CO2/N separations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the composite CMS membranes with a defect-free top polyimide layer can be successfully prepared and the CMS membranes prepared from the polyimides with thermally decomposable functional groups displayed higher gas permeances and higher gas selectivities.
the CMS composite membranes derived from the poly(amic acid)s with thermally decomposable sulfonic acid salt groups and/or –C(CF2)2– groups are promising for gas separation applications.
the CMS membranes prepared by pyrolysis of polyimides with thermally decomposable functional groups have great potential as the gas separation membranes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the composite CMS membranes with a defect-free top carbon layer of 1 to 2 μm thick could be prepared by pyrolysis of the precursor composite membranes.
the thermally decomposed groups in the precursor polyimides can be utilized to enhance the gas permeance of the resultant composite CMS membranes without compromising the ideal selectivity.
it is possible to obtain CMS membranes with high gas permeances by controlling the decomposition temperature of thermally decomposable functional groups in precursor polyimides.
